newsitem.title: INDIA: Chidambaram asks Indian institutions to take risks.
newsitem.headline: Chidambaram asks Indian institutions to take risks.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday India's leading domestic institutions should take more risks in their investment strategies.
He said share deliveries on the country's leading bourses, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE), were just a fraction of the total turnover.

"I am concerned that deliveries hover around 9.0 percent on the BSE and NSE. It means that most transactions are being squared," Chidambaram said at the launch of India's first share depository which will introduce paperless trading.
He said registered foreign insitutional investors were playing an important role but there were not enough large Indian players.
Chidambaram said organisations like the General Insurance Corporation, Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) and the Unit Trust of India (UTI) should reflect on the role they play.
"The government will not give directions to any of these organisations...but I urge financial institutions to take risks," Chidambaram said.
"Businessmen must take risks, within ofcourse, the statutes that govern them and existing prudential norms," he said.
In response to a question, Chidambaram denied asking local institutions like LIC to buy shares to prop up sluggish capital markets.
Market observers say the finance ministry often asks local institutions like UTI and LIC to buy index-lined stocks towards the end of a sluggish session to boost share prices.
